name: Maya Carter
signout: Six-day-old transferred for slow feeds and tachypnea. The cause is uncertain.

feeding.parent: She now takes less than half a bottle, sweats, and falls asleep during feeds.
feeding.nurse: Intake has fallen to less than half expected; she fatigues quickly.
feeding.label: Feeding

urine.parent: Only one wet diaper since this morning.
urine.nurse: Urine output has fallen over the last several hours.
urine.label: Urine output
urine.prompt: How many wet diapers has she had?

onset.parent: She seemed well after discharge, then became sleepier and breathed faster over about 12 hours.
onset.nurse: The decline has been progressive, not abrupt.
onset.label: Onset and progression
onset.prompt: When did this start and how has it progressed?

color.parent: Her feet look pale and feel colder than her hands. Her lips have stayed pink.
color.nurse: The lower extremities are cooler and more mottled than the upper extremities.
color.label: Colour and perfusion
color.prompt: Has she looked blue, pale or mottled?

breathing.parent: She breathes fast during feeds but has no cough or congestion.
breathing.nurse: Tachypnea is present without wheeze or prominent secretions.
breathing.label: Breathing
breathing.prompt: Is she working harder to breathe?

fever.parent: No fever at home and no sick contacts.
fever.label: Fever and exposures
fever.prompt: Has she had any fever or sick contacts?

birth.parent: She was born at 39 weeks after an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery.
birth.nurse: Term newborn with an uncomplicated nursery course.
birth.label: Birth and pregnancy
birth.prompt: How were the pregnancy and delivery?

findings.default: Ill-appearing but responsive newborn with weak cry and poor feeding endurance.
findings.deteriorating: Gray, lethargic newborn with weak cry and markedly reduced feeding endurance.
findings.postTreatment: More alert newborn with improved cry; feeding remains deferred during stabilization.

findings.default: Tachypnea with mild subcostal retractions; lungs are mostly clear.
findings.deteriorating: Marked tachypnea with increasing retractions; lungs remain mostly clear.
findings.postTreatment: Tachypnea persists but work of breathing is beginning to improve.

findings.default: Tachycardic regular rhythm with a soft systolic murmur and gallop.
findings.deteriorating: Marked tachycardia with gallop and a soft systolic murmur.
findings.postTreatment: Regular rhythm; the gallop is less prominent after improved systemic perfusion.

findings.default: Brachial pulses are 2+; femoral pulses are faint. Feet are cool and mottled with delayed capillary refill.
findings.deteriorating: Brachial pulses are present; femoral pulses are not palpable. Feet are cold and mottled with capillary refill over 5 seconds.
findings.postTreatment: Femoral pulses are now palpable but remain weaker than brachial pulses; feet are warmer and capillary refill is improving.

findings.default: Liver edge is enlarged below the right costal margin; abdomen otherwise soft.
findings.deteriorating: Hepatomegaly is more prominent with worsening congestion.
findings.postTreatment: Liver edge remains enlarged but is no longer increasing.

findings.default: Responsive to handling but tires quickly; tone is mildly reduced.
findings.deteriorating: Lethargic with reduced tone and weak response to handling.
findings.postTreatment: Responsiveness and tone are improving with perfusion.

findings.default: Right arm 68/42, left arm 66/40, right leg 48/28, left leg 46/26.
findings.deteriorating: Arm pressure 52/30; leg pressure is unobtainable by cuff.
findings.postTreatment: Arm pressure 72/44; leg pressure 58/34. A residual gradient remains.

findings.default: Right hand 95%; foot 91%. The difference is present but is not diagnostic by itself.
findings.deteriorating: Right hand 91%; foot 86% with worsening perfusion.
findings.postTreatment: Right hand 96%; foot 94%. The difference has narrowed.

orders.name: Cardiorespiratory monitoring and vascular access
orders.result: Continuous monitoring is active and vascular access is established.

orders.name: Point-of-care glucose
orders.result: Bedside glucose is 58 mg/dL. Hypoglycemia does not explain the current shock pattern.

orders.name: Blood gas and lactate
orders.result: Metabolic acidosis is present; lactate remains elevated.

orders.name: Blood culture
orders.result: Adequate-volume blood culture was collected before antibiotics; organism data are pending.

orders.name: Urgent transthoracic echocardiogram
orders.result: Severe discrete aortic coarctation with restrictive ductal flow, impaired left-ventricular function, and systemic hypoperfusion.

orders.name: Prostaglandin E1 infusion per neonatal critical CHD protocol
orders.result: Infusion has started. Systemic pressure, perfusion, pH, lactate, and respiratory status require close reassessment.

orders.name: Empiric parenteral neonatal sepsis coverage
orders.result: Empiric neonatal sepsis coverage has started while infection remains in the differential.

orders.name: Bring airway equipment and respiratory support to bedside
orders.result: Airway equipment and respiratory support are immediately available at bedside.

orders.name: Small cautious isotonic fluid aliquot with reassessment
orders.result: A small aliquot is complete; perfusion and respiratory status require immediate reassessment.

orders.name: Rapid large-volume isotonic fluid bolus
orders.result: Respiratory effort and hepatic congestion worsen after rapid volume expansion.
